issue.title: sase monitor start transfers the workspace claim from the newest lane member's pid, so a lane whose newest member is a settled monitor fails to start a second monitor
issue.description:
Discovered by epic sase-ku's exercises phase (sase-ku.10) and corroborated by the zo root-cause note on epic sase-ku. Filed by the sase-ku land agent; NOT caused by sase-ku (see root cause below).

SYMPTOM (two independent observations on lane sase-ku.10, 2026-08-13):
  1. 17:21:32Z - after a completed host-style monitor (e9m61z) on lane sase-ku.10, a second start created monitor brgjrd with starter_agent=sase-ku.10--mon and failed with stderr 'workspace #0 with pid 3700673 was not found'.
  2. 17:32:23Z - a retry with an explicit '--lane sase-ku.10' failed the same way: 'workspace #0 with pid 3702168 was not found'.
  3. The zo note on sase-ku records a third: sase-ku.10--mon-0 (artifacts 20260813132048, starter sase-ku.10--mon) failed at start with 'could not claim workspace: workspace #0 with pid 3700673 was not found' - a monitor started BY a monitor member.

ROOT CAUSE: src/sase/monitor/start.py:176-190. start_monitor() reads the NEWEST lane member's agent_meta.json ('raw_meta') and, when inherit_lane_workspace_claim is set and the cwd matches the lane workspace, unconditionally sets transfer_from_pid = raw_meta['pid'] and starter_agent = raw_meta['name']. There is no check that the newest member is a live agent runner rather than an already-settled monitor member. When the newest member is a '--mon' member, that pid is its DEAD supervisor's pid, so transfer_workspace_claim() at start.py:255-264 fails with 'workspace #N with pid <dead pid> was not found', _terminate_supervisor()/_teardown_failed_member() run, and start_monitor() raises MonitorError. The monitored command never runs.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT A sase-ku REGRESSION: git blame attributes 'transfer_from_pid = runner_pid' to b32167c31b ('feat(monitor): add monitor member lifecycle and supervisor process', epic sase-kp) and the surrounding guard to 44796037a5 / 10d3527dd5 - none of them sase-ku commits. sase-ku.4's transactional rewrite preserved the existing semantics.

SCOPE: decide the correct source for the claim transfer when the newest lane member is a monitor member. Options include skipping monitor members when picking the transfer source (walk back to the newest non-monitor member), verifying the recorded pid is alive before attempting a transfer (supervisor_is_alive()/process liveness already exists in src/sase/monitor/identity.py), or claiming fresh instead of transferring when the transfer source is not a live runner. Cover the regression with a test that starts a second monitor on a lane whose newest member is a settled monitor member.
